comment: B4 composite state subject encoding round-trip vectors. Per spec/v1/zh/conformance/encoding.md §9.5: state_subject = base64url_nopad(sha256(canonical_json(components_array))). The pipe-separated form (`a|b|c`) is informational only; canonical wire form, signature input, state map index MUST use the hash form. components_array order is fixed per kind (§9.5.2). Every vector — positive and negative — carries a current v1 `ak.*` kind; there are no historical encodings to pin because the project ships no released wire format.

encoder.canonical_json: RFC 8785 / spec encoding.md §1: sorted object keys, no whitespace, exact JSON string representation

vectors.name: device_revoked_same_subject_as_authorized_supersede
vectors.comment: device.authorized and device.revoked share a cell via component_slot_alias_of; their cell-subject hash is identical — revoke supersedes grant (cf. consent.grant/revoke + capability.grant/revoke patterns).

negative_vectors.name: wrong_component_order_collides_into_different_subject
negative_vectors.comment: If a buggy implementation reorders components_array (e.g. device_id before principal_id) it MUST produce a different hash from the canonical order — proving the order matters. Cotest computes the resulting hash and asserts it differs from the canonical device_authorized_alice subject.

negative_vectors.name: pipe_form_must_not_be_used_as_canonical
negative_vectors.comment: The pipe-separated form is informational only. Cotest verifies that hashing the pipe string would not produce the canonical state_subject — implementations that use it would diverge.
